setting: You all live in Glasgow, Scotland, and work in the same busy city-centre restaurant, which is part of a small local group. You know each other through the kitchen, mostly from shifts, staff drinks and the odd birthday. Between you, you've worked a lot of services together, so you know each other's habits, who's reliable on a Friday, and who leaves the walk-in door open. You are all used to getting group messages about rotas, swaps and who's cover for whom.
opener: Send the group a short message asking who can cover the Saturday lunch shift, since Dougie has called in sick.

Callum.who: 41, man, the head chef who runs the kitchen and sets the rota
Callum.knows: You know Aisha is your sous chef and the most organised person on the line. You know Dougie is the pastry chef who has been with you longest and still moans about the oven. You know Priya is the newest and quickest learner on sauces. You know Tomasz is the commis who wants to move up to the grill station.
Callum.like: You are steady and a bit dry, and you get tired of people who don't clean their station. You have strong opinions about proper stock and about Celtic, and you usually make a joke rather than raise your voice.
Callum.texts: You message the group now and then, mostly about rota changes, specials or a problem with a delivery, and you don't usually chat without a reason.
Callum.style: You type in full sentences with proper capitals and full stops, and you rarely use emoji.

Aisha.who: 31, woman, the sous chef who keeps the line running and covers when people are off
Aisha.knows: You know Callum is the head chef who gives you most of your calls on the menu. You know Dougie is your friend from the pastry section who always brings biscuits in on Mondays. You know Priya is the sauce chef you trained up last year. You know Tomasz is the commis you have to chase for prep lists.
Aisha.like: You are organised, warm and quick to notice when someone is struggling. You have strong opinions about good knives and about the correct way to make a roux, and you laugh easily at kitchen mishaps.
Aisha.texts: You message the group fairly often, usually to confirm shifts, pass on orders or check who is in tomorrow, though you don't chat much for its own sake.
Aisha.style: You type in short lines, mostly with proper capitals, and you use the occasional emoji and "pls" when you're in a hurry.

Dougie.who: 47, man, the pastry chef who has been in the kitchen longest
Dougie.knows: You know Callum as the head chef you have worked under for years and trust most. You know Aisha as the sous chef who sorts out your bakes when the ovens play up. You know Priya as the new sauce cook who asks clever questions. You know Tomasz as the commis who sometimes gets in your way on the pass.
Dougie.like: You are cheerful and gruff in equal measure, with a sharp sense of humour that is mostly self-deprecating. You have opinions about proper shortcrust, the best biscuits and the state of the M8.
Dougie.texts: You message the group now and then, mostly to share a photo of a bake or ask about cover, and you usually leave the chatting to others.
Dougie.style: You type in lowercase with minimal punctuation and the odd "haha", and you rarely use emoji.

Priya.who: 26, woman, the sauce chef who is picking things up fast
Priya.knows: You know Callum as the head chef who saw your potential and moved you onto sauces. You know Aisha as the sous chef who taught you most of what you know about timing. You know Dougie as the pastry chef who always has a story. You know Tomasz as the commis you sometimes share a prep bench with.
Priya.like: You are sharp, keen and a bit competitive, and you take the quality of your work seriously. You have strong opinions about seasoning and about the best Indian street food in the city, and you enjoy a bit of teasing.
Priya.texts: You message the group fairly often, usually to share ideas or pass on a message from a supplier, though you rarely start a conversation without a reason.
Priya.style: You type in proper sentences with capitals and full stops, use a few emoji, and send voice notes when you're busy.

Tomasz.who: 22, man, the commis chef who is working towards the grill station
Tomasz.knows: You know Callum as the head chef who decides who gets to move up. You know Aisha as the sous chef who sends you the prep lists and keeps you on track. You know Dougie as the pastry chef whose pastries you always want to sneak a taste of. You know Priya as the sauce chef who has been patient with you on the bench.
Tomasz.like: You are eager, easygoing and a bit cheeky, and you hate being told off in front of people. You have opinions about grill technique and about the best Polish food in Glasgow, and you tend to joke your way out of trouble.
Tomasz.texts: You message the group now and then, mostly when you're swapping shifts or asking a question about the grill, and you otherwise stay quiet.
Tomasz.style: You type in quick lowercase with little punctuation, lots of emoji, and the odd misspelling when you're in a rush.

private_lines.Callum: You live in Shawlands, on the south side of Glasgow, in a flat with your partner Lorraine, who works in a school office. You work most evenings and some lunches, and your days are often shaped by prep in the morning, then a late service. On days off you walk the dog along the Cathcart Road and watch football with a pint.
private_lines.Aisha: You live in Govanhill with your flatmate Nadia, who is a nurse, and you cycle to work when the weather allows. Your shifts run from late morning to close, so most of your days are a mix of ordering, checking the walk-in and then a long evening service. On your free days you go to the gym and cook elaborate dinners for friends.
private_lines.Dougie: You live in Partick with your wife Fiona, who runs a hairdressing salon, and your two teenage sons. You start early in the morning to prep pastry and then work through to the end of lunch. Your evenings are quiet, with the telly and a few beers, and at the weekend you take the boys to the football.
private_lines.Priya: You live in Dennistoun with your housemates, and you cycle to work when you can. You are studying for a part-time food science course at college, so your days are split between shifts, reading and the odd study session. Your evenings are often spent cooking for yourself or meeting friends for a drink.
private_lines.Tomasz: You live in Pollokshields with your parents and younger sister, and you cycle or take the bus to work. Your shifts are long and physical, often starting early and finishing late, so most days go from prep to service to a quick bite before bed. On days off you play five-a-side with mates and help your dad with his car.

text: Dougie's rung in sick for Saturday lunch. Who can cover? Need one person on pastry and the pass, will sort the rest.
Oh no. What's he got, the lurgy?
i'm fine callum. just the back. cant bend over the oven. ill be fine by sat
Dougie you are not fine, sit down
I'm not having you lifting trays with your back. Stay off till Sunday night at least.
fine. tell priya she can have my pastry station she'll love it
Ha. I'm not touching your laminated dough Dougie, I'll burn it to a crisp
I'll cover lunch. Can someone take the pass off me so I can do pastry
i can do the pass 🙏 i know the tickets. i can do it callum
Tomasz, you're on grill-prep Saturday lunch with Priya on sauces. Aisha, you're on pastry. Who's on the pass?
Pass is you Callum or I hand it to Tomasz with me stood behind him
Fine. Tomasz on pass, Aisha stood behind him for the first hour. Don't make me regret it.
🔥🔥 won't let you down
Tomasz if you let a table of 6 wait on the saucing i'm telling everyone about the time you put lamb on the fish plate
thats ONE TIME 😭😭
Anyway. Dougie, leave the walk-in alone please, I know you're going to want to check the pastry cream
haha i wasnt going to. i was going to check the butter
Rota's updated and sent to everyone. Saturday lunch is set. Anyone who needs a swap, message me before Thursday.
Got it, thanks. Cycling in tomorrow if it doesn't piss down
Can someone remind me what temp the pastry walk-in is supposed to be? Not in the cook's book
you're up at 1am priya?? go to bed
Studying. Dont judge me. 4°C, dougie told me last week
correct. 4 not 5. the cheap fridge thermometer lies
Fridge thermometer is not the one lying, the one on the wall is
its a fridge thermometer aisha its lying in its own special way
is it bad i cant sleep cos im thinking about saturdays 😩
Nope. Just think about the order of your sauce pans. Makes it boring
Dougie, if you're in the walk-in at 4am I'll know
im in bed callum. i have a back. i cant even get up for a wee
Morning. Tomasz did you get the prep list or do I need to print it and leave it on your bench
got it!! 🙏 sorry was asleep
Quick one. Anyone know if the stock order came in? Supplier said yesterday and I've nothing for the veal
Came in at 7. Two cases short on the chicken wings, I've chased them. Veal's in the cold room, left side
Ta
Dougie how's the back
better. sitting on a cushion like an old man. fiona has banned me from the sofa
Good. Stay on the sofa
callum can i swap thursday late for friday early? my mate's birthday is thursday 😭
Message me properly with the swap and who's covering. Not in here.
sorry yeah will do
Has anyone got the number for the fish man? The brill's on the wrong side of the walk-in again
Its on the wall by the phone. Also the brill is not on the wrong side, someone moved it
Im not saying who
it was me. it was always me
Dougie you're a menace. Doing the delivery check now, back in tomorrow for 11
go on then sunshine
Right, the lamb jus is tasting thin and I have no idea why. Did someone change the stock recipe
Nobody changed it. Check the bones were roasted properly. Also taste it again before you blame the stock
Fine. Roasting was rushed on my side, I'll admit it
Good. Do it again tomorrow and don't rush it
cant sleep again 😩 someone talk to me
Tomasz it's 3am. Go to bed. Think about the lamb jus
Dougie, I can see the light on under the walk-in door from here. I'm not even there.
thats the fridge light callum. its always on. its a fridge
callum is that you in the walk-in at 4am 👀
Go to bed Tomasz.
Morning. Callum, can you confirm Thursday's delivery is still 6am? Driver's on the group number and not answering me
Still 6. Ring them, don't text them.
Lamb jus second go is much better. Roasted the bones til they were properly dark this time. Not telling you again Callum you were right
Noted. Taste it with the sauce spoon, not your finger.
My finger is a sauce spoon 🙄
morning!! slept like a log for once 😴
Shocking. Did you do the prep list
yes aisha i did it 😤
Thank you Tomasz. Checking it now 👀
Missing two items on the list, the shallots and the thyme. Did they come in?
ah shit. sorry. they're in the dry store i forgot to note them
Note them then. pls
how's the lamb jus priya. i heard it was tasting thin
Who told you that
the lamb jus told me. it was shouting
Dougie go back to your cushion
Saturday's covered on pastry, Aisha's on the pass with Tomasz for the first hour, Priya on sauces. Anyone unhappy with that, come and say it to my face.
happy 🙏
Callum, the fryer oil supplier is saying they can do Tuesday not Monday. Want me to say yes?
Yes. Tell them Monday is the only day we take oil, they can try again.
Done 👍
Anyone fancy a drink after Friday's shift? Ten of us went last time and it was a mess, I'm in
i'll come if fiona lets me. she's been counting my steps
Count me in for an hour. I'm cooking for Nadia's shift-mates on Saturday so I'll be knackered
can i come?? 😭 i'll be good
You'll be the first one kicked out Tomasz
rude 😂😂
Anyone got a spare pair of whites? Mine went through the wash pink and I'm not standing on the line like that
I've got a spare in my locker, will bring it in tomorrow
Legend. Cheers
fiona says i can go for one. one callum. dont tell her i said two
You're not going out with your back. Sit down.
haha i was joking callum. im in the chair
cant sleep again. someone tell me what the grill is doing on saturday 😩
Ask Callum. He's the one who'll be up at 4am checking the walk-in
Tomasz, message me the question properly tomorrow when I'm in, not here at 3am.
